M3.reason: Parts the brief implies, checked in the views: barrel (LEFT, RIGHT), receiver (dark block at the middle of LEFT and RIGHT), wooden pump with grooves (RIGHT, and the ridged forend at the middle of BELOW), wooden stock (RIGHT, BELOW), trigger guard (notch under the receiver in LEFT), and a magazine tube (the second bar beside the barrel in TOP and BELOW). A front bead sight is not resolvable at this picture scale, so it is not charged as missing.

M4.reason: Black-grey metal on the barrel, receiver and muzzle, and warm brown wood on the stock and pump, matching the brief's black metal with wooden pump and stock. Regions match in every view, including the first-person and attack frames.

M5.reason: The pump's grooves and the receiver's ejection port are shown as painted detail at the scale the game draws. The brief asks for nothing more, and the reproduction adds nothing wrong.

M8.reason: The check passes with no errors. Triangles are 132 against Half-Life's median of 138, well under the limit. The muzzle is open, which is correct, and the stock, receiver, pump and barrel join with nothing floating in any view.

W1.reason: In the first-person view the asset sits low on the right side of the frame, where the game's own sits, held the same way round with the barrel pointing up and forward. Across the twenty attack frames the orange and dark gloves stay on the pump and receiver as the gun moves through the swing, and the gun does not leave the hands where both are seen.
